title: scalable-reserve-droplet-and-tenant-saturation-detector
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: production tenants with bursty traffic patterns occasionally drive node-level saturation that triggers aggressive autoscaler decisions and SLO violations for adjacent tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight per-tenant saturation detection signal and a small, bounded 'reserve droplet' allocation mechanism that provides short-lived, spillover capacity to tenants that are about to hit sustained saturation. The goal is to reduce noisy-neighbor-induced autoscale churn, protect tail latency, and improve utilization signals used by downstream accounting. Design summary: 1) Saturation detector: a new sampler that computes a tenant_saturation_score by combining per-pool occupancy, queue-depth percentiles (P90/P99), and recent scheduling rejections. The detector emits a short TTL score (30s window) and a smoothed score for admission logic. 2) Reserve droplet allocator: small reserved allocations (1-3 slot droplets depending on tenant tier) that are liquid — they are granted for short intervals (default 45s), charged to tenant allocation, and reclaimed aggressively on preemption. Allocation decisions are conservative: total droplets per pool capped at 8% of pool capacity and subject to headroom budget. 3) Autoscaler/Admission integration: the admission controller consults the tenant_saturation_score to prefer droplet granting over immediate scale-up when a tenant shows transient saturation but the cluster still has headroom. When cluster-wide pressure persists, the fallback is the regular autoscaler path. 4) Telemetry and reporting: exports tenant_saturation_score, droplet_allocated{tenant,pool}, droplet_preempt_count, and a derived tenant_saturation_class (OK/WARM/CRITICAL). These feed the utilization rollup and a new tenant-level heatmap in Console. Rollout plan and safety: staged rollout toggled by feature flag fleet.reserve-droplet.enabled. Canary on two non-critical us-west pools for 48h, then expand to 25% of pools with increased sampling. Safety knobs: hard cap on droplets per pool, per-tenant max-droplet-per-minute, and opt-out via tenant config. Backwards-compatible: if the feature flag is off, no control path changes. Linear/Jira: relates to ENG-3419 (reduce autoscale churn), PM-4128 (tenant latency regressions), and SUP-1221 (customer incident follow-up). Checklist: - [x] unit tests for detector scoring and edge cases - [x] integration test with admission controller sim in bench-lab - [x] telemetry metrics + Grafana dashboards (draft) - [x] migration docs and tenant opt-out documented - [x] e2e dry-run in canary region - [x] rollout feature flag and safe defaults Known limitations: detection window tuned conservatively; may under-react to extremely short microbursts (sub-100ms). Future work: adaptive droplet sizing, budget-aware droplet pooling across zones.
